interface.shortDescription: Turn your idea into a game
interface.longDescription:
Make a Game helps you turn a game idea into a real, playable game by chat, even if you have never written code: a browser game that plays on computers and phones, or a mobile game for iPhone and Android.

What you can do:
- Shape your idea: the type of game, the goal, the controls, levels, scoring, characters, look and sound.
- Check your game plan: paste your idea or design notes to get scores for six areas (concept and goal, gameplay and controls, levels and scoring, screens, look and sound, accessibility) and the most important missing pieces, in priority order.
- Get game code: a small browser game in HTML, CSS and JavaScript that you can play right away, or help fixing, explaining or extending code you have.
- Plan the screens a finished game needs: a title screen, how to play, pause, game over with Play again, and settings.
- Get a build link: answer 5 quick questions and get a personalized link that opens an online app builder with your game brief already filled in.

Great for: arcade, puzzle, quiz, word, runner, platformer, card and board games, party games and games to share with friends.

How the tools work: the game plan checker analyzes only the plan text you share in the conversation. It never opens web addresses, and the plans and briefs you send are not stored. The build link opens an online app builder with your brief and includes the plugin creator's affiliate code. Make a Game is an independent plugin by AI Research Plus.

Limitations: Make a Game writes plans, game briefs and code in the conversation. It does not host or publish games, create store accounts or submit games to app stores for you. Scores from the game plan checker are rough estimates based on the plan's wording.

The reply with the build link ends with a one-line sponsor disclosure.
capabilities: Turn a game idea into a playable game
Check a game plan for missing pieces
Write and fix browser game code

Open your game brief in an app builder

positive.description: Plan with no goal, ending or scoring
positive.prompt: Check my game plan: a space game where you dodge asteroids. Arrow keys to move.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the game plan checker with the plan text, reports the overall score and the six area scores as rough estimates, notes that the plan already has controls and obstacles, then gives the top fixes in priority order: a goal or win condition, how a round ends (lives or a timer) and scoring with a best score.

positive.description: Platformer plan missing a win condition
positive.prompt: Is my platformer plan ready to build? Pixel art, 10 levels, collect coins for points, jump with Space, 3 lives, a title screen, a pause menu and a game over screen with play again.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the game plan checker with the plan text, reports the scores (strong on levels, scoring and screens), then gives the top fixes: say how a level is won, add obstacles or enemies to overcome, and say how the levels get harder.

positive.description: Quiz game plan without answer controls
positive.prompt: Review my quiz game idea: a trivia quiz about world capitals for a quiz night with friends. Players answer 10 questions against a 15-second timer and get points for each right answer.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the game plan checker with the plan text, reports the scores (strong on the concept and goal), then gives the top fixes: how players answer (click or tap), how a round ends, and a results screen with the score and Play again.

positive.description: Mobile runner plan without touch controls
positive.prompt: What's missing in my mobile game plan? An endless runner for phones where a cat runs across rooftops and jumps over gaps.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the game plan checker with the plan text and platform mobile, reports the scores, then gives the top fixes: touch controls for phones (tap or swipe), a goal or win condition, and how a run ends.

positive.description: Puzzle game plan missing how levels are solved
positive.prompt: Check this puzzle game plan: slide colored tiles to match patterns, 30 levels that get harder, stars for fewer moves, calm music.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the game plan checker with the plan text, reports the scores (strong on levels and difficulty), then gives the top fixes: what solves a level, how tiles are moved (drag, tap or keys), and whether a level can be failed, such as a move limit or a timer.
